why:
issue 1942 (2026-10-26) — SHIPPED; was `gap`. `nros::ServiceInfo` (`packages/core/nros-core/src/service_info.rs`) is rclrs's per-request service metadata: `request_id` (`RequestId { writer_guid: [u8; 16], sequence_number }` — the client's GID and the client-assigned sequence number, upstream's `rmw_request_id_t`) and `source_timestamp` / `received_timestamp`. A callback receives it beside the request through `Node::create_service_with_info` or `node.service(name).service_info().build(..)` — `FnMut(&Request, &ServiceInfo) -> Reply`.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: rclrs fills all three, non-optional, timestamps as `SystemTime`.

OURS, AND THE CONSTRAINT: every field is an `Option`, and the timestamps are `nros::Time` — no `SystemTime` without `std` (no_std). Whether a request carries a field is a BACKEND property, and a backend that cannot say leaves it `None` rather than inventing a value — the `MessageInfo` precedent. Measured per backend: zenoh reports `request_id` and `source_timestamp` from the query attachment (`rmw_zenoh_cpp`'s layout, which our client writes too), and no `received_timestamp` (the query carries none). Cyclone, XRCE and every other C-ABI backend report nothing: the C `take_request` slot carries only the reply-correlation token (`rmw_vtable.h`: `seq_out` "stands in for `rmw_service_info_t`"), issue 2081. A Rust backend's info crosses that slot through the adapter's side table (`store_cffi_service_info`).

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: the `Option` is a compile-time difference; which backend fills which field is in the type's module rustdoc (the envelope), and `ServiceInfo::is_reported()` says whether the backend reported anything at all.

HIDDEN UNTIL phase-506 W1: the facade re-exported the RMW seam's service DESCRIPTOR (`nros_rmw::ServiceInfo`) under this name and the correlator matched them. The seam now re-exports this type as `nros_rmw::ServiceRequestInfo`, so the two never share a name again.
